readsAs: sun setting in a valley between two rounded hills or standing stones
two tilted tombstones with an orange disc between them
two leaning figures sharing a sun, or an abstract lowercase 'i' shape
judge.why: The sun-in-the-vale idea suits the name, and plum with amber avoids the corporate-green look, but the tilted round-topped dark slabs read strongly as gravestones, which works against an optimistic, trustworthy co-op; the odd nick on the smaller slab's shoulder also looks unresolved.

readsAs: market-stall awning or shop canopy
small stool or table with a scalloped skirt
a shopfront or bakery icon
judge.why: The scalloped awning is tidy, warm and holds up well at small sizes and in one colour, but it reads as a retail market stall or shopfront icon rather than neighbours co-owning solar roofs, so it says nothing about energy, roofs or shared ownership and looks like a stock shop glyph.

readsAs: chunky warm serif 'Sunvale' with an orange sun-dot on the S
the letter S with a rising sun or ball behind it
friendly, retro-leaning local co-op or food brand
judge.why: The aubergine-and-amber soft serif feels optimistic and clearly not corporate-green, but the disc on a letter is a familiar move. In black and white versions the disc merges into the S as a blob, and in the wordmark it leaves an awkward gap between S and u that reads as 'S unvale'.

readsAs: the numeral 4 or a stylised letter A
a sailboat sail with a boom
a sundial gnomon casting a shadow
judge.why: The sundial is a clever way to show the sun without rays, and the plum and amber colours are pleasantly not corporate-green, but at a glance the mark reads first as a '4' or a sail, nothing in it suggests neighbours co-owning roofs, and the white keyline with its rounded corner looks heavy and slightly awkward against the thin shadow blade.

readsAs: generic user/profile avatar (head and shoulders)
sun dropping into a cupped valley or bowl
camera or webcam icon
judge.why: The sun-in-a-valley idea suits the Sunvale name and holds up from 16px to 256px and in one colour, but the shape reads first as a stock user-avatar or camera glyph, which will cause real confusion as a members' app icon and leaves little that Sunvale can own.

readsAs: a swoosh curling around a dot, like a sun in a valley
a snail or tadpole shape
an ear or a sideways question mark
judge.why: The plum and gold colours avoid the corporate-green look, but the swoosh-and-dot is a generic shape that reads as a snail or ear rather than neighbours co-owning solar, and the kinked joint where the hook meets the tail weakens the craft.

readsAs: warm lowercase serif wordmark with a u–n ligature
the letters 'un' (a negative prefix, or French for 'one')
generic editorial or bookshop type in coffee brown
judge.why: The brown serif wordmark feels warm and avoids corporate green, but the u–n ligature is too subtle to be ownable and leaves a rough notch at the baseline join, and the 'un' icon cut from it doesn't point to Sunvale, reads as a negative prefix and carries no idea of shared roofs or co-ownership.
